html:
The battle in 202 BCE, in what is now Tunisia, in which a Roman army under Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal and ended the Second Punic War.

Hannibal had spent fifteen years in Italy. When Scipio invaded Africa, Carthage called him home. Scipio had won over the Numidian prince Masinissa, whose cavalry gave the Romans the edge in horsemen. Hannibal opened with some 80 war elephants, but Scipio left lanes in his lines so that many passed through harmlessly. The infantry fight was hard, and was decided when the Roman and Numidian cavalry came back and struck Hannibal's rear.

Carthage asked for peace. In 201 BCE it gave up Spain and its other lands abroad, handed over its fleet except for ten ships, paid a large indemnity over fifty years, and promised not to make war without Rome's leave. Rome was now the leading power of the western Mediterranean. Fifty years later it destroyed Carthage altogether.
sum: The battle in 202 BCE, in what is now Tunisia, in which a Roman army under Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal and ended the Second Punic War.
